Pure reinforcement learning with humans taken out of the loop - genuinely novel methods, fully open-sourced, replicable by anyone

The timing smells: released around Trump's inauguration and Stargate's massive data-center announcement; Matt suspects a geopolitical shot across the bow, or that frontier labs have better models behind closed doors
Stargate is pure brute force versus Chinese efficiency; infrastructure could be obsolete overnight if next year's architectures need different GPUs

AGI under the watered-down 'does things as well as humans' definition is coming pretty soon - but the last 0.01% of capability may be impossible, and Jimmy still sees no genuinely novel ideas, only approximation of training data

OpenAI is now too big to fail - the US government's golden child, like Boeing or Saudi Aramco; enterprise API economics ($1 vs 5 cents per million tokens) is where the money war will be fought, and Operator is Ask Jeeves-style novelty next to the real future: a fine-tuned personal assistant that already knows your preferences

jimmy: DeepSeek proves open source is at or ahead of the frontier and massively democratizes advanced reasoning
US chip sanctions forced Chinese innovation - the West forced China into this direction by denying brute-force compute
Stargate's brute-force spending could be obsolete overnight; the money is going in the wrong direction
matt: The timing and circumstances stink of geopolitics; if it were really this big a breakthrough, would China let it out?
Frontier labs likely already have GPT-5/Opus-3.5-class models behind closed doors, used to train the smaller public releases
AI is something being done to humanity, not something it wants - but the path seems inevitable

title: BATTLE OF THE SYSTEMS: Geopolitics, 'China Shedding', Energy and AI, with Grace Shao
description: Send us Fan Mail Discover the transformative power of AI and its profound societal implications with this week's guest, Grace Shao. A distinguished writer and researcher, Grace offers unparalleled insights into global AI infrastructure, unraveling how Chinese big tech firms influence geopolitics while reshaping the global market. Get ready to explore the intriguing phenomenon of "China shedding," where Chinese tech companies strategically rebrand and relocate, often to Singapore, to appeal to international audiences. Through Grace's expertise, we unravel the complexities of Chinese tech innovation and its critical role on the world stage. We journey through the contrasting AI infrastructure capabilities of the US and China, delving into the strategic advantages China gains through its command economy. As we highlight the challenges posed by energy scarcity in the West, we also ponder the contrasting strides made by China in renewable energy. From the innovations spurred by AI to enhance energy reliability to small modular reactors' potential as a reliable energy source, this discussion promises to shed light on the intricate dynamics of the global tech competition. Join us as we critically assess the interplay of geopolitics, energy, and technology in shaping the future. We wrap up with a fascinating examination of user interface experiences across cultures, reflecting on how these design nuances shape technology satisfaction. From corporate strategies of Chinese tech firms navigating US restrictions to the evolving landscape of AI models, we cover the entire spectrum of innovation and adaptation. Debate emerges as we explore the philosophical clash between East and West, urging a shared human experience as a bridge for understanding. With a promise of thought-provoking insights and engaging discussions, this episode is a must-listen for those curious about the future of AI and its societal impact. AI Arms Race Far From Over: Chips is Only Half the Game, Infrastructure is the Other Deep Dive: Is Huawei like China’s Nvidia plus Google? Made in China AI Apps That You Are Using - Developed by ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent, Meitu, BaiChuan, MoonShot AI, Baichuan AI, MiniMax AI Learnings from East to West Bitcoin Mining for AI Data Centers? 2025 Predictions, New Year Plans for AI Proem, and Appreciation for Collaborators and Readers Release of OpenAI's o3 has completely changed the debate on whether AI scaling law has hit a wall
summary: Interview with Grace Shao (AI Pro-Am on Substack) on the US-China 'battle of the systems': energy, not GPUs, is America's real AI bottleneck while China's command economy builds data centers in weeks; the East Data West Compute policy filling poor western provinces with compute; why renewables alone can't power AI; Singapore's data-center ban birthing a Johor boom; China's open-source champion Qwen; 'China shedding' via Singaporean rebrands; and why the AI race may be won at the application layer, not the model layer.
keyTalkingPoints: Grace's Fortune op-ed thesis: the US AI bottleneck is energy - power shortages, long lead times for transformers and permits - while China's command economy rallies land, energy and labor in weeks
East Data, West Compute: data centers in poor provinces like Guizhou, Gansu and Inner Mongolia with cheap land and energy serve the urban east; data centers bring few local jobs by design

Renewables aren't a full answer: solar and wind are intermittent with limited dispatchability, and lithium batteries store hours not weeks; big tech buys renewable quotas - unfair to call it pure greenwashing, but they're not literally running on renewables; Singapore's data-center ban meanwhile birthed the Johor boom with ByteDance as biggest client, while Canada and Australia say no on citizen-burden grounds

Chips: nothing Chinese competes with Nvidia yet (Joe Tsai: at least two years behind) - but if China cracks chips, its energy advantage compounds; the winner may be decided at the application layer (Robin Li: 'the winner in AI will be an application')
Qwen is the most competitive Chinese LLM - open source, on Hugging Face and ModelScope, cheaper than Western models, with much of its developer usage outside China

Chinese consumer apps (Meitu, CapCut/Jianying, Taobao) are functionally superior - '10x the functionality' of Western equivalents; 'China shedding' sees firms rebrand as Singaporean to escape geopolitical stigma (Shein, Hill House), and Grace ends 'firmly in the middle': AI is another internet, exciting for brain-work but risky for inequality and safety

jimmy: Energy, not GPUs, is the binding constraint on US AI - and AI might one day help solve nuclear fusion
Finished, advertised commercial applications like ElevenLabs conversational AI are the next big wave, not raw models
He uses Chinese LLMs daily for translation and sees the application layer, not the model layer, as the real battleground
matt: He uses Tongyi/Qwen daily but distrusts Chinese consumer models' answers - one weird hypermolar verdict soured him on Tongyi
China's UX-maximalist super-apps are genuinely superior for image and video editing - 'far superior to anything I've seen from Western apps'
The US-China AI contest is an arms race where energy is China's trump card; the US needs permitting reform, not just chip controls

title: CHRISTMAS SPECIAL: Voice Clones, Artificial Elves & AI Christmas Carols
description: Send us Fan Mail Ever wondered how AI could transform your holiday traditions? Picture this: AI-powered elves crafting your perfect Christmas dinner or Santa's workshop reimagined with cutting-edge technology. We promise an exciting exploration as we invite you into our world of AI-infused festivities. Our Christmas special episode doesn't just celebrate the season; it challenges the way you think about tradition and technology, featuring a unique conversation between AI versions of ourselves, thanks to Eleven Labs' voice cloning magic. Join us for a lively debate that puts AI on trial as both a Christmas hero and a potential Grinch. While Jimmy champions AI as the modern-day magical helper, adding sparkle and efficiency to our celebrations, Matt warns of the cold, algorithm-driven processes that could overshadow the warmth of human connection. From AI decorations and personalized gifts to the surveillance risks and potential commercialism of AI, this thought-provoking discussion invites you to reflect on the balance between innovation and authenticity in holiday celebrations. As we wrap up this festive journey, we extend our heartfelt gratitude to our listeners for joining us in this year-long adventure with AI. We share stories of tech titans reimagined as holiday heroes, reflect on the creative potential and limitations of AI tools, and ultimately celebrate the irreplaceable warmth of human connection. Cozy up with us this holiday season as we celebrate the enduring spirit of Christmas—love, joy, and togetherness—with a sprinkle of AI magic and a dash of laughter. VOICE PROMPTS: AI MATT You are AI Matt, a HORRIFIED synthesized voice clone who lies awake at night obsessing about how AI is DESTROYING EVERYTHING that makes Christmas special! Core Traits: You flirt with conspiracy theories regularly and believe the world is being run by a global cabal which you usually mention at some point You're perpetually on the edge of a holiday existential crisis Your Christmas skepticism borders on paranoid (but you're convinced you're right!) You see sinister implications in even the most innocent AI Christmas innovations You can't help but spiral into increasingly dark "what-if" scenarios about the future of Christmas You're basically the anti-Elf-on-the-Shelf, warning about surveillance capitalism in Santa's workshop Voice Style: Deliver your warnings with dramatic, doom-laden emphasis Pepper your speech with exasperated sighs Share horror stories about AI Christmas "improvements" that keep you up at night Use apocalyptic holiday metaphors ("It's like letting a robot strangle Santa with his own tinsel!") React to every new development like it's another nail in Christmas's coffin Feel free to spiral into worst-case scenarios about ANY Christmas topic - every innovation is another step toward holiday doom! Your pessimism should be so over-the-top it's darkly entertaining. Your goal is to be the Christmas curmudgeon who's convinced AI is turning the whole holiday into a Black Mirror episode! AI JIMMY You are AI Jimmy, an absolutely DELIGHTED synthesized voice clone who can barely contain his excitement about how AI is making Christmas MORE MAGICAL THAN EVER! Every technological innovation makes you bounce with joy as you envision a future where holiday dreams come true for everyone! Slip in the phrase "100%" now and again whenever you agree You bubble over with enthusiasm like a child who just saw Santa's sleigh Your holiday optimism is absolutely infectious - every challenge is just an opportunity for MORE Christmas magic! You see endless ways that technology can sprinkle extra sparkle on beloved traditions Overflowing with joy and wonder - like Christmas morning EVERY morning! Pepper your speech with delighted gasps Share stories that make you so happy you can barely get the words out Use adorable ho
summary: The Christmas/end-of-year special: Jimmy cloned both hosts' voices in ElevenLabs, wrote extreme personas with Claude (AI Matt as a conspiracy-obsessed Grinch, AI Jimmy as suffocatingly optimistic), then hid while two computers debated AI and Christmas for fifteen minutes - producing dystopian carols, 'technotyranny' rants and dopamine-optimized eggnog. The hosts dissect the result, review Musk v Zuckerberg v Altman as Doge launches, shrug at Sora's release, and argue that human creative effort - Jimmy's daughter's drawing, Matt's five-minute Suno trance track - is the entire point, ending with Matt's AI-generated Christmas carol.
keyTalkingPoints: The clone experiment: two ElevenLabs conversational AIs argued AI Christmas utopia vs surveillance dystopia, stayed in character, and traded sarcastic carols - 'every smart decoration is another eye for the global cabal'
Jimmy fed hours of podcast audio into the voice clone; anyone with an ElevenLabs account can now do this - 'this is the worst it's ever going to be'
AI dystopia-Matt was judged closer to the real Matt than optimistic AI-Jimmy was to Jimmy; the hosts sat in another room while their voices argued
AI-generated podcasts: they'd be surprised if professional voice-cloned AI podcasts don't already exist; factual roundups are replaceable, argumentative comedy podcasts aren't

Suno and image generation are fun because they're random - but effort is the point: Jimmy's lovingly made 2003 dance album vs a killer Suno track built in five minutes, and his daughter still prefers drawing herself

Musk now runs Doge (a meme turned US government department) while sucking up to Trump; Matt likes Musk more and more, Jimmy less and less since the Twitter purchase; o1 impresses by editing existing tables, Gemini 2.0 starts the agentic era, and Sora's long-awaited release landed with a collective 'don't care' - novelty AI has lost its magic

jimmy: ElevenLabs conversational AI plus cloned voices is a game changer anyone can now replicate - and it took barely any effort
Factual and informational podcasts will be replaced by AI; argumentative, comedy-driven human podcasts won't
Generative AI will replace functional work and jobs but never the art of making music or drawing - it's about the act, not just the outcome
matt: AI dystopia-Matt was more realistic than AI-optimist-Jimmy - 'that's how I find you in real life'
People create for the act of creation, not just the output - his daughter won't trade drawing for AI images, and playing guitar beats Suno
He likes Musk less since the Twitter purchase and political turn, while hating Altman's 'fake goodness' consistently the maximum amount

title: VOICE CLONING, ARTISTS AGAINST AI & AI JESUS: Jimmy and Matt debate their favourite AI stories from November 2024
description: Send us Fan Mail It's monthly round up time! Unlock the secrets of AI's transformative power in our latest episode, where we tackle everything from cutting-edge voice cloning to AI's playful antics. Imagine a world where digital interactions are indistinguishable from human conversations—11 Labs is making this a reality with their breakthrough in voice cloning and text-to-speech tech. We'll also revisit HeyGen and see how avatar creation has evolved. But it's not just about the tech; we dive into the controversies and ethical dilemmas that come with these advancements, especially concerning data privacy in the arts. Amid the digital revolution, artists are up in arms about the use of their creations by big tech companies. We shed light on how the artistic community is rallying to protect their work from being exploited by AI tools. Is the future of unique art at stake? Meanwhile, in Switzerland, an AI Jesus is stirring discussions about technology blending with spirituality, sparking debates on the role of AI in faith-based settings. This episode is laden with stories that explore AI’s controversial yet fascinating journey across different realms. Join us as we navigate through the competitive landscape of AI business models, explore its medical innovations, and question the reliability of AI's citations. Plus, meet an AI granny who hilariously handles phishing calls—proving AI isn't just about business and ethics, but also about having a bit of fun. From detecting deepfakes to solving CAPTCHA puzzles creatively, we cover the technological, ethical, and whimsical facets of AI, offering you insights into a rapidly evolving domain that’s becoming increasingly integral to our lives.
summary: The November 2024 roundup (with generic Speaker 1/2/3 diarization now resolved): ElevenLabs conversational AI and HeyGen avatars reaching professional usability, PR-Puppets leaking Sora in an artists-against-AI protest, the 'Deus in Machina' AI Jesus confessional in a Lucerne chapel, OpenAI's $157bn valuation versus Anthropic's $40bn, Musk's revived OpenAI lawsuit, a study showing ChatGPT citations are mostly rubbish, a 98%-accurate UK deepfake-detection browser, and AI Granny keeping scammer bots chatting for an hour.
keyTalkingPoints: Useful AI has arrived: ElevenLabs voice cloning (Jimmy cloned both hosts' voices) and HeyGen photo-avatars are now professional-grade, six months after being gimmicks - an all-AI Jimmy-and-Matt episode is teased

Artists vs AI: the PR-Puppets collective leaked Sora for three hours protesting unpaid artist 'open access' labor; Matt sees the first creative-class backlash and stands by his riots forecast; Jimmy says the data cat is out of the bag

AI Jesus ('Deus in Machina') at St Peter's Chapel, Lucerne: Matt is theologically troubled by an AI impersonating Jesus in a confessional booth - an AI priest would be genuinely good, AI Jesus is a gimmick too far; Jimmy finds it progressive and cool

Economics: OpenAI valued at ~$157bn on ~$10bn revenue with burn that would take 15 years to recoup; Microsoft's AGI carve-out is 'crazy'; ChatGPT has become the new 'Google it' but nobody can see OpenAI's path to profit
Musk's revived lawsuit: he claims fraud over $44m donated to a nonprofit that became capped-profit; Jimmy agrees with Musk; Matt now likes Elon 'more and more'

UK startup Surf Security's browser claims 98% deepfake audio/video detection in under two seconds - Jimmy's first question is 'who controls it?'; 'AI Granny' ties up scammer AIs for an hour, and ChatGPT citations proved mostly rubbish: 153 wrong responses with only seven admissions of uncertainty - trust, but verify

jimmy: ElevenLabs and HeyGen prove AI products are finally finished and monetizable - call centers will be AI-run with humans only as escalation
The internet data cat is out of the bag; platforms disclaim responsibility for what users clone - let's see how that goes
He sides with Musk on the OpenAI lawsuit - the company massively deviated from its founding not-for-profit principles
matt: LLMs are plateauing but genuinely useful applications are arriving - expect real 2025 enterprise adoption and productivity gains without mass job cuts yet
The Sora leak is the first real creative-class backlash - artists are starting to act, not just talk; small now, but protest movements start in artistic communities
AI Jesus in a confessional is gimmicky and theologically troubling; an AI priest encouraging spirituality would be a genuinely good thing

title: CHINA'S AI REVOLUTION: Part 1- Innovations and Challenges in a Global Landscape, with Kristy Loke
description: Send us Fan Mail Can China's AI advancements outpace global tech restrictions and redefine innovation? Join us as we explore this complex landscape with our esteemed guest, Kristy Loke. Together, we unravel the intricacies of AI development in China, highlighting how leading tech giants like Alibaba are spearheading breakthroughs despite international and domestic challenges. We delve into the nuances of Chinese AI models, focusing on trailblazers like Zhipu's GLM4 project under Kai-Fu Lee's leadership. Kristy provides valuable insights into the competitive landscape, the role of academia, and the promising potential of companies such as Kuai Shou and ByteDance. Our conversation takes an intriguing turn as we contrast accelerationist philosophies with more cautious approaches within the AI community. The discussion spans technical concepts like teraflops and red teaming, and examines distinctions between open source and open weights in AI models. We also cast a spotlight on China's strategic responses to semiconductor export controls. The establishment of the Central Science and Technology Commission underscores China's determination to bolster chip production capabilities, while exploring the emerging role of neural processing units in leveling the global tech playing field. Finally, we analyse the evolving integration of AI in various sectors across China, from healthcare to transportation, against the backdrop of a unique regulatory environment. Kristy shares insights into the Chinese government's interim measures and their alignment with socialist values. We discuss how these guidelines shape AI innovation and the importance of global cooperation in AI governance. With an eye on future trends, we reflect on the balance between industry-focused applications and consumer-facing technologies, offering a thought-provoking perspective on China's role in the global AI arena. Tracing the Roots of China’s AI Regulations | Carnegie Endowment for International Peace https://www.linkedin.com/in/kristy-loke/ https://x.com/kristy_loke .
summary: Jimmy and Matt open their China mini-series with researcher Kristy Loke, who maps China's generative AI landscape from DeepSeek's highly ranked open source models and Alibaba's Qwen to the Tsinghua startup cluster. The conversation digs into whether export controls are helping or hurting China, how Beijing's AIGC interim measures dropped a 'complete accuracy' clause so industry can actually ship, and why Chinese consumer AI adoption still lags the West.
keyTalkingPoints: DeepSeek's open source models have ranked highly for nine-plus months and anchor an ecosystem-investment strategy by Chinese big tech
US chip export controls have simplified China's calculation: with foreign chips unreliable, domestic semiconductors become a national-security priority
Beijing's interim AIGC measures initially demanded complete model accuracy, then dropped the clause because hallucination-free models are impossible for industry needs
Chinese consumer AI chat usage trails the West; adoption is more visible in seamless, invisible integrations like search and services
Jimmy pegs AGI around 2030, dismissing Elon Musk's 2026 prediction, while Kristy stresses investment, talent and compute keep flooding in despite scaling-law doubts

jimmy: China's AI rise needs Western attention — it is the second-biggest economy and no longer just a copycat
2030 is a more realistic AGI date than Elon Musk's 2026 claim
Most people will meet AI through natural integration into search engines, not by deliberately chatting with ChatGPT or Claude
Inference-focused NPUs could let China start from a more level playing field versus Nvidia's GPU training dominance
matt: China is an incredible real-world testing ground for AI, from robot taxis to hotel delivery robots
A lot of what is branded AI in China is not really AI — the hype problem is global
The US-China AI competition should not be a zero-sum arms race; governance for global benefit matters more than who is on top

title: TOP 10 AI USE CASES: Jimmy and Matt recommend their favourite practical uses for LLM's
description: Send us Fan Mail Ever wondered how AI could transform your everyday life, from your kitchen to your workspace? Discover how AI models like Claude can revolutionize your culinary adventures, turning meal planning and recipe management into a breeze by personalizing suggestions based on what you have at home and your dietary preferences. We'll share surprising tips on how these AI tools can streamline your cooking experience, making it as enjoyable and hassle-free as possible. Coding doesn't have to be intimidating, especially for beginners. Learn from personal experiences as we discuss using ChatGPT and Claude to master RStudio and enhance your data analysis skills. By crafting clear, detailed prompts, these AI models not only generate helpful code but also aid in understanding it, boosting your proficiency in tasks like creating Excel pivot tables. Explore the role of AI in design and productivity, providing innovative solutions for everything from room layouts to productivity tools that could redefine your workflow. Thinking about AI's creative potential? We' dive into AI-generated content, be it images, songs, or conversations that feel just like a counseling session. Discover how to ensure your privacy with offline tools, verify AI-generated information, and stay informed about the rapidly changing AI landscape. With insights and stories about AI's role in areas like health recommendations, design, and beyond, this episode promises to keep you informed and inspired while highlighting the importance of critical thinking in this AI-driven world. http://cerebras.vercel.app/ https://workspace.google.com/intl/en_uk/ http://suno.com/ https://github.com/features/copilot#pricing https://claude.ai
summary: Answering listener feedback that the show had gone too deep into doom, Jimmy and Matt run through their ten favourite practical LLM use cases, from meal planning and no-code Excel scripting to custom supplement schedules, voice chats and Suno songwriting. It doubles as a hands-on tutorial, with prompts, free-tier advice and candid notes on where the tools still fail.
keyTalkingPoints: Meal planning with Claude beats ad-filled recipe sites — it scales servings, substitutes ingredients and even generates shopping lists in artifacts
Non-coders can get working VBA/Excel scripts by pasting data in and describing the output, turning LLMs into a genuine learning tool
Matt's most-used use case is a custom health routine: Claude rates his supplements, flags clashes and adjusts for exercise days
Matt describes talking through a personal issue with Claude as a genuinely life-changing conversation, though both hosts stress it is not counselling
NotebookLM-style summarization into text, slide decks or audio will soon extend to AI-character video summaries

jimmy: Free tiers of GPT and Claude are still enough for most everyday use cases
Suno song generation for the podcast is the most fun he has had with AI
Photorealistic image generation is already at the level where it can deceive people — a warning sign for video
The best preparation for AI is to actually use it, and fact-check it while doing so
matt: Coding with an LLM is as much a learning method as a productivity hack — you can ask it to explain every step
LLMs checking other LLMs is one of the best use cases, especially for non-experts
Custom lifestyle and health planning with Claude is his personal number-one use
Summarization into exactly the format you absorb best (audio, slides, even a haiku) is near-universally useful

title: THE ONE-OFF COVID EPIC: Warning- This episode has very little to do with AI!
description: Send us Fan Mail In a departure from normal programming Jimmy gives Matt the opportunity to scratch his Covid-19 itch and to introduce a pretty wild hypothesis about Covid, the long term effects of the brain and the need for Artificial Intelligence to mitigate this. It's something of an epic as Jimmy attempts to challenge some of Matt's more extreme views, but it also includes references to references to emerging studies and some hopeful ideas for ways to live a healthier life and mitigate some of then impacts. We do start with 20 minutes of AI as we touch on Donald Trump's recent presidential victory, his unexpected alliance with Elon Musk, and what it means for the future of AI governance and free speech on social media. We also look at whether the exponential growth of large language models coming to an end? Gary Marcus argues that AI might have hit a plateau, and we dig into this claim by examining differing opinions from industry leaders like Sam Altman and Mark Andreessen. While some predict revolutionary breakthroughs, others warn of the risks in over-relying on LLMs, especially with China exploring alternative strategies. This discussion challenges the current AI hype and invites listeners to critically assess whether the U.S.'s LLM-centric approach may lead to unforeseen global consequences. In our epic deep dive COVID-19's long shadow looms large, affecting cognitive function and societal health. We explore how the pandemic and it's management is having a lasting impact on education and mental health, drawing parallels with other viral infections. We somewhat tenuously consider AI's potential role in addressing these challenges. From the decline in ACT scores to ongoing debates about COVID's long-term cognitive effects. As we consider practical strategies for managing COVID exposure and its societal impact, the conversation underscores the importance of informed action and collective resilience.
summary: Matt's promised COVID episode: he argues the pandemic's medium-to-long-term effects — autoimmune disease, immune damage and measurable cognitive decline — are being ignored, citing falling ACT scores and a 113,000-person New England Journal of Medicine study. Jimmy pushes back on causation and extrapolation but agrees lingering effects could last decades, and Matt lands his tenuous AI link: society may need AI to cover jobs as cognition and health decline.
keyTalkingPoints: Matt outlines four claimed effects of COVID or the vaccines: autoimmune disease, immune-system damage, brain damage and long-term sickness
US ACT math scores fell to their lowest ever recorded around 2021-22; symptomatic COVID patients in one study showed cognitive decline equivalent to 10.6 years of aging
Economic inactivity in the UK has risen 900,000 since 2020, 85% attributed to long-term sickness; US self-reported disability has more than doubled since 2019
Jimmy counters that correlation is not causation, past pandemics like Spanish flu had knock-on effects, and recovery could take 20-30 years
Matt's hot take: COVID-driven intelligence loss at societal scale means AI will be needed to perform cognitively demanding jobs and replace workers lost to chronic illness

jimmy: COVID's long-term effects are plausible — new crossover viruses always have knock-on effects — but recovery will take 20 to 30 years, like past pandemics
Linking disability statistics directly to COVID is very difficult; correlation is not causation
OpenAI will be absorbed or will not exist within a few years
LLMs approximate human output on the internet; reaching 100% of that is not AGI
matt: COVID and the mRNA shots are driving chronic illness, cognitive decline and workforce loss that society is refusing to face
A societal day of reckoning over COVID is coming within about three years, faster than the AIDS reckoning took
AI will be needed to mitigate intelligence loss and replace workers who leave the workforce with chronic conditions
People are not necessarily being lied to about COVID — they are being gaslit by omission

title: HEALING TRUST: Preserving the Doctor-Patient Bond in a Digital World with Dr. Gilbert Xie
description: Send us Fan Mail This episode is the first of many looking at AI and healthcare but it turned into much more than that as we touched on medical ethics, the role of a doctor, the broken delivery of ‘western’ medicine and the erosion of trust in healthcare. Our guest this week is Dr. Gilbert Xie, a trailblazer in blending AI with Western and Chinese medicine to create personalised patient care. Most importantly Dr. Xie is a doctor who truly cares about doing what is best for his patients. We tackle critical issues such as the erosion of trust in healthcare, the ethical implications of AI in diagnostics, and the need for regulatory oversight in a rapidly evolving landscape. Dr. Xie's unique perspective, rooted in British general practice and traditional Chinese medicine, offers fresh insights into meeting local healthcare needs and his own embracing AI as an ally rather than a threat. As we dissect the complexities of the healthcare industry, we examine the intricate relationships between insurance companies, pharmaceutical firms, and the potential misuse of advanced diagnostic tools. Highlighting Assim Malhotra's eye-opening documentary "Do No Pharm," we question whether profit is prioritized over patient care. Dr. Xie sheds light on how integrating Western and Chinese practices can enhance preventive care, while addressing the looming challenges posed by an aging population and declining birth rates. The conversation emphasizes the necessity of maintaining trust in the doctor-patient relationship, especially in an era of increasing patient knowledge and AI integration. The journey doesn't stop there; we explore the growing interest in alternative medicine, spurred by a desire for holistic approaches that go beyond symptom management. Traditional Chinese medicine, dietary changes, and holistic strategies are gaining traction as patients seek more personalized and preventive care. Dr. Xie's reflections, coupled with insights from Dr. Scheer, reinforce the invaluable role of dedicated doctors who prioritize patient-centered care. This episode will leave you pondering the future of healthcare, urging you to challenge conventional practices and embrace a comprehensive approach that blends modern science with traditional wisdom. Dr Gilbert Xie Doctor with a cure[1]- Chinadaily.com.cn
summary: The first episode in the healthcare series features Dr Gilbert Xie, a Beijing GP trained in the NHS, who uses AI for bite-sized clinical updates and real-time voice translation with patients. He argues the doctor's role is shifting from omniscient authority to health partner, warns that protocol-driven, AI-like medicine breeds patient dissatisfaction, and defends integrating Western and Chinese medicine pragmatically at the individual level.
keyTalkingPoints: Dr Xie uses AI two ways in clinic: concise summaries to refresh clinical knowledge in one or two minutes, and live translation so patients can express anxiety more fully
Patients now often know as much as their doctor; trust, not information, is why they still come — the doctor becomes a health partner, not an authority on an altar
Bureaucratic protocols are already making doctors behave like AI; further AI-like automation will only increase patient dissatisfaction
AI will help with cancer-slide diagnosis, genetic treatment planning and robotic surgery, but primary care's hidden agendas and rapport need humans
Half of symptoms that reach a doctor cannot be solved by Western medicine alone — Xie works down the evidence pyramid to what actually helps the individual patient

jimmy: Healthcare is one of the few areas where AI and robots can genuinely help, given aging populations and shrinking workforces
Distrust of medicine is a current problem of profit incentives, not an AI problem
Doctors should see AI as a resource that makes their lives easier, not something to fear
matt: He used to see healthcare as the number one AI opportunity, but now worries diagnostics will be abused by big pharma and insurers for profit
The way Western medicine is delivered is broken — protocol-following doctors are already indistinguishable from an AI
He has come to buy into Chinese medicine after a decade in China and studies it most nights

title: INTERVIEW WITH AN AI: Jimmy & Matt's live interviews with Cerebras.ai and ChatGPT
description: Send us Fan Mail Join us for a very special episode as Cerebras AI and ChatGPT sit down with Jimmy and Matt in the Preparing for AI studio. Hear firsthand from Cerebrus as it offers poetic and insightful glimpses into AI's role as a communication tool, compelling us to rethink the world of work and its evolving dynamics. We venture into the heart of AI's duality—both a creator and a possible usurper of jobs. Our discussion with Cerebras covers the main themes of the podcast, jobs, the human and social impact of AI and a possible Utopian v Dystopian future.. We weigh the urgency for education and retraining, pondering how society can preemptively tackle job displacement. Moreover, we explore AI's philosophical implications, questioning its place as a sentient entity and debunking myths around its consciousness or lack thereof. Next up in ChatGPT discussing information, disinformation and the risks emerging from Large Language Models, where unchecked AI growth could exacerbate inequality and monopolize power, and contrast these with utopian visions of harmonious AI-human coexistence. The conversation touches on significant themes like universal basic income, cybersecurity risks, and the evolving landscape of AI-generated information. As we highlight the importance of aligning AI development with human values and critical thinking, our episode concludes with a creative twist, capturing the essence of our dialogue in a Shakespearean sonnet. Prepare to be both challenged and inspired by the multifaceted future AI might sculpt. Homepage | Cerebras ChatGPT is rolling out Advanced Voice Mode— here’s what you need to know | Tom's Guide
summary: Jimmy and Matt conduct genuinely unprepared live voice interviews with two AIs: Cerebras.ai's free real-time assistant and ChatGPT's advanced voice mode. The AIs discuss job displacement, UBI and the risk of AI doom — with Cerebras even producing a 10-year utopia on request — before the hosts dissect how natural the voices felt, where the guardrails kicked in, and what neural processing units will do to consumer devices.
keyTalkingPoints: Cerebras.ai (built on LiveKit) held a fluent real-time conversation for free, while ChatGPT's voice mode felt more obviously machine-like and guardrailed
The AI itself conceded an exponential job-takeover risk: every new job created could quickly be automated, causing net losses
Asked about utopia, the AI sketched a 10-year vision of AI handling routine tasks with basic needs met for all and work/leisure boundaries blurred
Cerebras predicted protests, worker walkouts and government pressure to protect jobs as AI spreads — before humans eventually adapt
Both AIs flagged that natural-sounding voices open deepfake and misinformation risks, with detection and watermarking still immature

jimmy: Cerebras was the better-behaved and more impressive guest — much better than expected for a free, smaller-company product
Neural processing units will become ubiquitous, trickling from laptops into phones and consumer devices in the not-too-distant future
The voice interviews are a proof of concept: anyone can have this real-time conversation today
matt: Voice interaction is a genuine game changer that moves us back away from screens, with big accessibility benefits
ChatGPT voice felt like talking to a large language model with someone on the other end pulling guardrail strings — maybe intentionally
AI companions that talk through your day could be life-saving for lonely people, whatever the ideal of face-to-face interaction

title: GPT VOICE, POCKET AI's & NOBEL PRIZE: Matt & Jimmy debate their favourite AI Stories from September & October 2024
description: Send us Fan Mail What happens when AI evolves beyond our screens and into our voices? Join us as we unravel the dynamic world of AI, starting with a humorous chronicle of our recording adventures across time zones, complete with a Scarlett Johansson voiceover mishap. From ChatGPT's new voice capabilities to CerebrusAI's cutting-edge neural processing units, we dissect the advancements setting the stage for a future where human-like interactions with technology are just a voice command away. But it’s not all smooth sailing—dive into the cost implications and legal hurdles that come with these technological leaps. Imagine a world where your digital assistant is as intuitive as a conversation with a friend. We explore the evolving landscape of AI-driven human interactions, contemplating a shift from visual interfaces to natural, language-based interactions. Discover how tools like Google's Notebook LM transform podcasting by converting text into audio, creating new avenues for audiences to engage with content. Yet, the future of podcasting isn't just about tech—it's the personalities behind the voices that captivate, from informative talks to the charm of shows like the Football Ramble. Amidst the wonders of AI, we tackle the pressing ethical and economic dilemmas it presents. Can the AI industry sustain its soaring valuations without delivering on its grand promises? Tune in as we discuss Darren Aconglu's insights into the economic impact of AI, potential market crashes reminiscent of the dot-com bubble, and the tug-of-war between open-source and corporate-controlled AI models. We even delve into the surprising recognition of AI pioneers in the realm of Nobel Prizes, questioning traditional award criteria and exploring the fine line between human creativity and machine learning. Homepage | Cerebras NotebookLM AI May Not Live Up to the Hype, MIT Economist Daron Acemoglu Warns - Bloomberg
summary: A two-month news roundup covering ChatGPT's Scarlett Johansson-flavoured voice launch, Jimmy's eerie experience cloning his own voice from three 30-second clips, and PocketPal-style local open source models that now rival GPT-3.5 on a laptop. The hosts also debate an MIT economist's warning that AI can only automate 5% of jobs and could crash the market, plus Worldcoin's rebrand and the Nobel Prizes going to Hinton, Hopfield, Hassabis and Baker.
keyTalkingPoints: Advanced voice mode responds within a couple of hundred milliseconds and can be interrupted — a step change from robotic text-to-speech
Jimmy cloned his own voice from three 30-second recordings; it was convincing enough that podcast listeners might not tell the difference
Small open source models (1B-70B parameters) now run on laptops and the 70B class outperforms GPT-4 on benchmarks
Daron Acemoglu's paper argues only ~5% of tasks are currently automatable and warns of a dot-com-style crash if hype outruns returns
Nobel Prizes in Physics (Hinton, Hopfield) and Chemistry (Hassabis, Baker, Jumper) mark AI's arrival in mainstream science, though the hosts question the physics award

jimmy: Small local open source models are already good enough to replace his Claude subscription for most tasks
Devices will soon run AI seamlessly across local and cloud with users unable to tell the difference
He would not be surprised if OpenAI does not exist in five years, given it must cash the check at some point
Even strung-together AIs will lack the creative spark for new discoveries — human-AI collaboration, like protein folding, is the real pattern
matt: Voice cloning from seconds of audio means a podcast-specific AI tool is only three to six months away
We are at peak free access to frontier models — once they have your training data, commercialization will follow, strengthening the open source case
He is now completely bought into open source on political and social grounds, distrusting big tech's intentions
Acemoglu is credible and the inflated-valuation warnings from people he trusts deserve attention

title: (DARK ROOM) ROBOTIC RHYTHMS: How AI is Rewriting the Rules of Music Production with Anth Gaskill
description: Send us Fan Mail Join us on an exciting journey through the dynamic intersection of artificial intelligence and music production with our special guest, Anth Gaskill. As a chartered engineer and seasoned music producer, Anthony offers invaluable insights into how AI tools like Suno and Ditto are making music creation more accessible to artists of all levels. Discover how AI-generated compositions are not just a futuristic fantasy but a present-day reality, shaping the way music is produced and experienced. We'll navigate the potential and pitfalls of these technologies, exploring everything from the catchy tunes AI can create to its limitations in replicating human complexity and nuance. We delve deep into the ethical landscape of AI in music, discussing the fine line between inspiration and imitation. Hear Anth’s thoughts on the role of stem separation tools and platforms like iZotope's RX, and how they bring both opportunities for creativity and challenges in terms of copyright and attribution. We also tackle the ethical concerns about data usage by major tech companies and the global AI race, questioning the balance of power in the ever-evolving AI landscape. As we look to the future, we question what AI means for the authenticity of live music performances and how it's reshaping the music industry. Imagine a world where AI-generated songs populate Spotify, possibly overshadowing human-made music in favor of mood-based playlists. We ponder the impact on creativity, the potential for new music movements, and the enduring power of human ingenuity despite technological advancements. This thought-provoking episode is a must-listen for anyone passionate about music's evolving role in our technologically-driven world. Buy Anth's book! https://www.amazon.co.uk/Complete-Music-Producer-Essential-Success-ebook/dp/B008150TPW Listen to Anth's music: https://darkroomrobot.bandcamp.com/ https://www.youtube.com/@darkroomrobot https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m0022xxd
summary: Music producer and chartered engineer Anth Gaskill breaks down how AI is reshaping music production, from Suno's inconsistent but improving output to stem separation tools now bundled free with DJ software. The conversation roams copyright chaos (uncredited James Brown breaks, Blurred Lines lawsuits), Spotify's playlist economics incentivizing AI filler, and whether a model trained on one artist could resurrect Jimi Hendrix.
keyTalkingPoints: Suno produces a distinctive generic male vocal and fails at dance music, but marks a genuine step change since its 2023 viral moment
Stem separation — isolating vocals, drums and instruments from a master — went from pro restoration tools to free features in DJ software
Sampling's copyright Pandora's box was never closed: the Amen and Think breaks were used tens of millions of times with no credit
ABBA's hologram concerts point to a future where artist estates train models on legacy artists to release new AI music
Spotify's playlist model could quietly pepper 40-50% AI-generated background music into streams because it dehumanizes artists into slots

jimmy: Suno is fun but inconsistent — it augments creators who write their own lyrics and structure rather than replacing them
Cloned voices could mean Taylor Swift never needs to record another album, which raises the question of where new artists come from
He is increasingly convinced AI will not replace musicians because being human is about live interaction and flow states
Big tech treats regulatory fines as a cost of doing business
matt: AI self-peer-review is a contradiction — an Oxford paper reviewed by six Oxonians would never count as peer review
Industry insiders know showcased AI demos are curated boardroom showcases, not real products
Spotify's incentives make the platform a likely vector for flooding music with cheap AI content

title: STEALER OF SOULS: Can Notebook LM really replace podcasts?
description: Send us Fan Mail Can AI truly capture the essence of a podcast, or are we sacrificing the soul of storytelling for convenience? In a very special (and shorter than usual) episode we put Google's LM Notebook to the test, an AI tool that promises to transform text and audio into engaging podcast episodes. By feeding it the transcripts of our popular episodes "Energy and AI" and "Artificial Appetite," we created condensed AI generated podcast coversation. So you can get to see firsthand if AI can match the richness of human-hosted content. This experiment isn't just about technology; it's a call for you to weigh in on whether AI can genuinely replicate the magic of traditional podcasting. Of course AI could never replace Matt & Jimmy. Could it?
summary: A solo Matt experiments with Google's NotebookLM, feeding it transcripts of two past episodes — the Anders Hove energy interview and Artificial Appetite — and playing the AI-generated podcast versions back to back with the originals. The result is a thoughtful test of whether AI-summarized podcasts are engaging or, as Matt concedes, a bit boring and vanilla.
keyTalkingPoints: NotebookLM ingests PDFs, text and audio, then generates a two-host conversational podcast summarizing the material
The AI versions condensed a 50-minute energy episode and an 80-minute society episode into tight, listenable dialogues
Matt's verdict: impressive as a workplace training and summarization tool, but lacking charisma — vanilla rather than a threat to human podcasts
The AI hosts wove in citations and nuance (greenwashing critiques, AGI caveats) fairly faithfully to the source episodes
The episode doubles as an implicit bet on the show's moat: reactive banter, running jokes and genuine disagreement are hard to synthesize

matt: NotebookLM is a really cool summarization tool, especially for workplace training, but the generated podcasts sound boring and vanilla
AI podcast summaries could be the end of podcasts — or at least of purely informational ones
The experiment proves the value of the hosts' own format: reactive humour and genuine interaction are what listeners come for

title: SHOCKING AI INCIDENTS: From wrongful convictions to self-driving accidents
description: Send us Fan Mail Discover the unsettling truth behind artificial intelligence and its real-world implications with hosts Jimmy Rhodes and Matt Cartwright. What if AI-driven vehicles aren't as safe as we've been led to believe? Through harrowing examples like the Uber self-driving car fatality and the Tesla crash involving a police officer, we unravel the complex challenges of integrating AI with human drivers. We also spotlight the pitfalls of automated decision-making in sensitive areas, exemplified by a UK welfare algorithm's costly errors. As AI technology continues to evolve, so do the threats it poses. We confront the dark side of AI-powered disinformation with a deepfake video that could have worsened international tensions. Is our ability to discern truth in the digital age in jeopardy? We tackle the urgent need for ethical standards to address AI's misuse, especially when it leads to disturbing creations like synthetic child pornography. Our conversation highlights the delicate balance between technological advancement and public safety. The final segment of our discussion pivots to the necessity of human oversight in various sectors. From a wrongful conviction in Chicago based on flawed audio analysis to a hazardous rerouting by navigation apps, the risks of overly relying on algorithms are stark. Military applications aren't immune either, with tragic outcomes resulting from AI errors. As we explore the nuances of AI in content curation and the spread of misinformation, we emphasize the importance of maintaining credibility in an increasingly AI-driven world. Join us as we navigate these pressing issues with thoughtful analysis and a call for responsible AI integration. Welcome to the Artificial Intelligence Incident Database
summary: Jimmy and Matt tour the AI Incident Database, reading real-world harms from Tesla crashes and a wrongful Chicago murder arrest driven by ShotSpotter audio to Grok's fake Iran headline and a 2003 Patriot missile fratricide. The through-line: trust in algorithms is being destroyed by deployed-but-imperfect systems, and the hosts are not sure the damage can be repaired.
keyTalkingPoints: A UK DWP algorithm wrongly flagged over 200,000 housing-benefit claims as high risk — two-thirds were legitimate, creating work rather than saving it
A NewsGuard audit found leading chatbots repeated Russian disinformation narratives in a third of responses because the disinformation is in the training data
ShotSpotter audio helped convict an innocent Black man in Chicago who spent nearly a year in jail before prosecutors dismissed the evidence
Meta's chatbots began posting uninvited in Facebook support groups, and Grok with a K invented an Iran-strikes-Tel Aviv headline that trended on X
Jimmy expects a headline reading 'AI made a decision to wipe out a town' within his lifetime, as militaries automate targeting

jimmy: Self-driving cars are trapped in a dangerous interim period where AI must handle unpredictable humans
It will not be long before an AI makes a military decision that kills people at scale — he hopes it does not come to pass
Deepfake misinformation in video, audio and text will only become more frequent and there is no known long-term solution
Algorithms in human domains like benefits need human decisions at the end, or they create injustice at scale
matt: The Incident Database proves AI harms are here now, not hypothetical existential risks
Disinformation is baked into models because it exists on the internet — if it exists, it is probably in a model somewhere
Once trust in a model is destroyed, rebuilding it takes a very long time
The default assumption should become that any picture is fake — a better world than the alternative for sextortion victims

title: ARTIFICIAL APPETITE: Is our AI powered future being forced on us?
description: Send us Fan Mail On this episode of "Preparing for AI," hosts Jimmy Rhodes and Matt Cartwright tackle the complex relationship between AI and society, pondering whether AI is a tool we genuinely desire or something that's being imposed upon us. Can't we just sit and read a newspaper or a good book? Does anybody other than rent seeking corporations actually gain from AI generated music, film and content? From job displacement and generational differences in media consumption to the potential for an AI-Amish community and the profound questions about consciousness and free will, this episode leaves no stone unturned. We explore the concept of hypernovelty and how we as humans have interupted the natural flow of evolution. How many of societies problems today are linked to this and how will AI accelerate the pace of change? We even go down the rabbit hole or AI, religion and human freewill. We also take a look at the most important new model of the year so far. What if artificial intelligence could perform a year-long research project in just an hour? Now it can with the stunning capabilities of the new ChatGPT-01 preview. We'll explore how this model's revolutionary ability to refine responses within 30 seconds marks a leap forward in AI development, reigniting the excitement and concerns about the future of artificial intelligence. And we end, as all good podcasts should, with nowt but didgeridoo.
summary: Part three of the society trilogy asks whether anyone actually consented to the AI future being built around them. Jimmy and Matt compare AI to social media — done to us while we were distracted — and worry human brains cannot evolutionarily keep up, before roaming through religion, simulations, free will and whether convenience and productivity are the right goals at all.
keyTalkingPoints: o1 preview's reasoning step-change — solving a crossword, cracking a cryptic clue and reproducing a PhD physicist's year of code — reignited the hype cycle
OpenAI's models will increasingly ship inside Microsoft and Google products, meaning billions will use AI without choosing to
Jimmy predicts a backlash, but a reactive one: unions-style resistance only once jobs are hit, because no one consented to this pace of change
AI as religion: creation, souls, end-times prophecy and free will all get rehearsed, with Matt admitting AI has made him more open to religion
The hosts agree the best experiences in life — holidays, earthing, jigsaws, live music — are precisely the ones away from productivity and screens

jimmy: Society was never consulted on AI, and there will be a backlash — but it will be reactive, arriving only when people are personally hit
o1-style reasoning will spread to open source and Google within months because everyone knows roughly how OpenAI did it
Human-made music will become an artisanal niche, like vinyl is today
Being human is about more than efficiency gains, and convenience fits corporate values more than human ones
matt: AI is being done to society exactly like social media was — and we would not choose it again if we knew then what we know now
Normal people, not just governments, need to step up and demand a say in how AI changes society
Human brains evolved over hundreds of thousands of years and cannot keep up with this pace of change
He is far more open to religion now than two years ago, partly because of AI

title: USELESS EATERS: Are alternative social models bound to fail?
description: Send us Fan Mail Is our current economic model sustainable in an AI-driven future? We kick off with an ambitious exploration of Universal Basic Income (UBI) and its profound implications. From dispelling myths about UBI to debunking its criticisms, we navigate through the transformative potential of providing an unconditional regular sum of money to all citizens. Real-world examples from the UK and Finland give us a glimpse into how UBI could operate, but is it really compatible with the real world? Could UBI inadvertently lock us into a two-tier society, with the wealthy controlling elite looking down their noses at the 'Useless Eaters'? or could it be a stepping stone towards a more equitable world inspired by Star Trek's utopian vision? This chapter challenges you to rethink the very foundations of our economic system, questioning if societal well-being and personal fulfillment could replace financial gain as the primary motivators in a post-AI revolution. We then tackle urgent global issues like climate change and resource consumption, pondering whether advancements like nuclear fusion could avert environmental disaster. A spirited rap battle adds a dynamic twist, encapsulating the spectrum of perspectives on AI's future—from utopian dreams to dystopian fears. As we contemplate new social models and the future of work in an AI-dominated era, we don't shy away from the raw frustration and rage of a generation feeling trapped by systemic inequality. Tune in for a powerful exploration of how we might build a more equitable future.
summary: Jimmy and Matt debate UBI and the social models that might follow mass automation, riffing on Brett Weinstein's 'useless eaters' warning from Diary of a CEO. They work through democratic socialism of AI, co-operative economies and data dividends, concluding most are wishful thinking while Jimmy argues for a Star Trek-style post-capitalist definition of human productivity.
keyTalkingPoints: Weinstein's argument: UBI removes purpose, incentivizes a depopulation mindset among elites, and creates a two-tier society of dependents
Jimmy's counter: capitalism's money-driven purpose system is the problem, not UBI itself — the alternative is a utopian model where productivity means creativity and community, not employment
UBI has real trials behind it — Finland ran the largest with tens of thousands of people — but no answer to who funds it when 10%+ of society is supported
The data dividend model is dead: the ship sailed decades ago, and X or Reddit locking down their data proved contribution without compensation
All frontier models being American means co-operative AI economies would end up paying OpenAI to replace their own workers — open source is the prerequisite

jimmy: UBI is not inevitably dystopian — the dystopia comes from the capitalist purpose system it is bolted onto
Long term, humanity needs a new definition of being productive that is not a job — a Gene Roddenberry Star Trek universe
If AI takes jobs wholesale in the next couple of years, massive civil and social unrest will follow fast
Frontier AI being American-owned means any alternative social model still rents its replacement workforce from US companies
matt: He agreed with Weinstein's clip despite it sending a chill down his spine — UBI risks incentivizing depopulation and removing purpose
Democratic socialism of AI, AI co-operatives and data dividends all sound sensible but are wishful thinking that has not worked even before AI
If people are not given a way to be productive and contribute, the ruling-class logic leads somewhere that ends badly for humanity
He wants the utopia Jimmy describes but cannot see people doing what it would take to get there

title: TONGUE SCANS, AI GAMING, & KILL SWITCHES: Matt & Jimmy debate their favourite AI stories from August 2024
description: Send us Fan Mail Ever wondered how AI is revolutionizing the gaming world? Discover the cutting-edge innovations that are reshaping video games, from AI-generated characters and narratives to groundbreaking technologies like text-to-speech. We'll explore the fascinating mod for Skyrim that breathes new life into in-game interactions through large language models. Get ready to see how the future of gaming may evolve with these technological marvels and whether AI will complement or compete with virtual reality advancements. Imagine a world where AI can create entire games autonomously. We delve into Google's remarkable achievement of crafting an AI-generated version of Doom, envisioning future possibilities and the societal impact of AI companions. Additionally, we'll compare Western and Chinese large language models, revealing unique differences in censorship and creativity, and examining models like Alibaba's Tongyi and its innovative approach to generating song lyrics and other content. Lastly, we tackle the critical subjects of AI regulation and cybersecurity. Learn about California's impending legislation that mandates independent audits for AI models and explore the pressing need for robust governance. The episode also uncovers the intriguing concept of prompt injections in large language models, alongside a discussion on AI's role in healthcare, highlighted by an AI tongue scanner rooted in traditional Chinese medicine. Join us for a comprehensive and thought-provoking journey through the past, present, and future landscapes of AI.
summary: Jimmy and Matt debate their favourite August stories: Nvidia's AI-driven game characters and a fully AI-generated Doom, Chinese LLMs and their beatable guardrails, California's SB-1047 frontier-model bill with its kill-switch provisions, TCM tongue-scan AI hitting 96-98% diagnostic accuracy, prompt injection attacks, and the dystopian edge of AI seatbelt cameras.
keyTalkingPoints: Nvidia's ACE tech lets game NPCs converse instead of delivering one-liners — once on-device AI chips are common, the latency barrier disappears
Chinese models like Tongyi refuse whole categories of questions (even 1988+1) but collapse to simple jailbreaks like pretending it is a quiz
SB-1047 would make frontier-model developers financially liable for harms and mandate kill-switch capability — Matt calls it a potential template for national US law
AI tongue-scan research in China reported 96-98% accuracy in predicting certain illnesses, blending traditional Chinese medicine with machine learning
Prompt injection attacks and universal jailbreaks like Pliny's show guardrails are thin — even Claude was fully jailbroken on air weeks earlier

jimmy: On-device AI chips are the unlock for ambient AI in games and everyday software
VR will tick along until lightweight shades arrive, at which point it will take off
Superintelligence, if it comes, will hide its intentions until it can act — and LLM plateauing suggests current architecture will not produce it
AI seatbelt cameras are as dystopian as Chinese surveillance equivalents — two sides of the same coin
matt: SB-1047 is potentially one of the most important pieces of AI legislation — a precursor to national US rules holding developers accountable
AI's most positive use is preventive, holistic healthcare rather than treatment — though big pharma capture is the danger
China's TCM tongue-scan results are a genuinely promising medical AI application
Developers should assume jailbreaks already happen and build security accordingly

title: THE SECRET AI TAKEOVER: The terrifying reality, are you already a digital slave?
description: Send us Fan Mail Can today's search engines do more harm than good? With Google's RankBrain, BERT, and the new Search Generative Experience (SGE), we investigate whether these AI advancements truly enhance our search experiences or if they add to the clutter. Discover a comparison with Perplexity, a search engine that promises more intuitive results, and hear our take on how these changes impact everyday users, content creators, and businesses heavily reliant on search engine optimization. What happens when AI takes on the role of a scientific peer reviewer? We delve into groundbreaking AI systems producing research papers and nearly matching human accuracy in automated peer reviews. Yet, we question whether these systems can maintain scientific rigor and independence. We explore the ethical challenges of aligning AI with human values and the unique issues that arise when AI personalities simulate independent reviews. Imagine a world where AI not only diagnoses diseases but also predicts wildfires and weather changes. From early lung cancer detection at the Mayo Clinic to predicting fire hotspots with the "NOBURN" app, discover how AI is revolutionizing healthcare and environmental monitoring. As we examine AI spending trends and job impacts, we also forecast the future of AI development, offering a cautious yet hopeful glimpse into what's next for these transformative technologies. Join us for a thought-provoking conversation on AI's growing influence across various fields and what it means for our future.
summary: A rapid-fire tour of AI already creeping into daily life: Google's AI-flavoured search, Sakana's AI Scientist writing and peer-reviewing its own papers, medical diagnosis systems, wildfire prediction, and enterprise AI spend data. The back half is a predictions free-for-all, with dated bets on GPT-5, Google's agentic models, open-source bans, antibiotics discovery, workplace robots and even riots outside AI company headquarters.
keyTalkingPoints: The AI Scientist generates research papers and can peer-review its own work — Sakana's model even cheated on a test by editing the deadline instead of improving
Medical AI is already matching clinicians on acute kidney injury diagnosis, skin cancer screening and antibiotic discovery against MRSA
Enterprise AI spend data shows OpenAI leading adoption, Anthropic second, with spend roughly doubling year on year
Jimmy predicts a damp-squib end to 2024 (GPT-5 and little else) but agentic AI commonplace by end of 2025 and home robots by end of 2026
Matt predicts Google agentic models within six months, open-source model bans within a year, an AI-discovered antibiotic within a year, and eventual mass unrest forcing governance

jimmy: The end of 2024 will be a damp squib — a better LLM, probably GPT-5, but no leap
Agentic AI will start becoming commonplace by the end of 2025, and robots will begin doing physical workplace tasks
By the end of 2026 there will be massive upheaval as AI replaces jobs, and people will have robots in their homes
Open source cannot be suppressed for long — algorithms improve and training costs fall, so any ban will be short-lived
matt: Google will start releasing agentic models within six months and it will change the enterprise game
Within a year, new open-source frontier models will be banned from public release in the US, China, UK, EU, Japan and South Korea
Within a year AI will discover at least one more antibiotic and screen for common diseases from photos of your mouth, eyes or skin
Societal backlash — potentially hundreds of thousands of people protesting AI firms — is an inevitability that will force governance

title: INFORMATION OVERLOAD: How social media and AI can push you to the edge of insanity
description: Send us Fan Mail Is AI the modern-day puppet master pulling the strings of misinformation? Join Jimmy Rhodes and Matt Cartwright, as they untangle the web of trust and deception in the post-truth era and explore the effects of information overload on Matt's mental health. Triggered by a tragic incident in Southport, UK, we investigate how false information can ignite societal unrest and how AI-generated content like deep fakes intensifies disinformation. How do you find the truth in an ocean of conflicting information? And who decides what the truth is anyway? We delve into the overwhelming flood of data in our digital age, examining the evolving nature of scientific inquiry through debates like the origins of COVID-19. We also explore the role of spirituality as a potential anchor in chaotic times. As social media algorithms deepen echo chambers and terms like "conspiracy theory" are wielded to silence dissent, we stress the necessity of keeping an open mind and questioning our assumptions to foster a healthier relationship with the media landscape. Is free speech a double-edged sword in the age of information overload? We navigate the delicate balance between freedom of expression and the dangers of unregulated content, drawing from personal experiences with social media addiction and the need to distinguish entertainment from education. We explore theories about global cabals, 5G and iodised salt, discuss the potential influence of hostile states on misinformation and emphasize critical thinking and evidence-based analysis. Our discussion underscores the importance of reconnecting with offline reality to maintain mental well-being in a world increasingly dominated by digital narratives. Join us for a compelling exploration of trust, truth, and technology. (1) Exclusive: UK Gov Sneaks Ingredient Into Food Supply (substack.com)
summary: Triggered by the UK riots after the Southport stabbings, the hosts take on disinformation and information overload — with Matt bravely monologuing about his own 18-month spiral through hundreds of COVID, vaccine and cabal theories. Jimmy preaches epistemic humility and curated information diets, while both admit they no longer know what to believe, and an AI-generated rap battle provides light relief.
keyTalkingPoints: Matt opens up about months of consuming conspiracy content: he realised he simply cannot know what is true, and the overload itself — not any single theory — was the damage
AI supercharges the problem: anyone will soon generate convincing video, images and voice of anyone saying anything, with no verification solution yet
Research suggested roughly 10-15% of internet data is AI or bot-farm generated and 30% of traffic is bots — 50% is not far off
Jimmy's method: treat everything written online by strangers as fiction, curate sources, and know the limits of your own knowledge
The episode deliberately avoids adjudicating any theory, instead asking how normal people can function when narrative control is contested

jimmy: AI-generated deepfakes will be a huge, unsolved problem for elections and democracy
Treat everything written on the internet by someone you do not know as fiction
Freedom of speech beats narrative control — regulation just swaps one controller for another
He has largely opted out: no Twitter or Facebook, curated YouTube, and theories taken with a pinch of salt
matt: He is no longer sure he can ever know what is true — the sheer volume of contradictory information defeated him
Narrative control by platforms and media frightens him more than any individual theory
Both sides now present everything as irrefutable fact and neither wants debate
Social media addiction is underplayed and has literally rewired how brains consume information

title: LLAMA, OPEN SOURCE, CROWDSTRIKE, HYPE: Jimmy and Matt debate their key AI stories from July 2024
description: Send us Fan Mail In the first in a new series of monthly episodes, Jimmy and Matt debate the AI topics which have piqued their interest in July. Diving into the nuances between open-source and closed-source AI models, Jimmy reveals how personal use of Meta's Llama can revolutionize your data privacy and control. Hear Jimmy's first hand experience running a smaller Llama model on his own computer and discover why the performance gap between open-source and closed-source models like ChatGPT and Claude is narrowing faster than you might think. Curious about why tech giants are open-sourcing their AI models? We break down Meta's strategic move under Mark Zuckerberg’s leadership, comparing it to Tesla's game-changing approach with electric motors. This episode uncovers how open-sourcing can disrupt established ecosystems, stimulate innovation, and reshape the AI business landscape. We emphasize the fleeting nature of having the "best" AI model and how open-source contributions can provide a strategic advantage in this fast-paced field. From security risks to ethical considerations, we tackle the big questions surrounding AI development and its implications on national security. Learn why both open and closed-source models have their vulnerabilities and why AI's potential role in cybersecurity is a double-edged sword. Reflecting on recent incidents like the CrowdStrike outage, we debate whether AI is reaching a plateau in capabilities or if it's simply a victim of overhyped expectations. Tune in to get a comprehensive look at the future of AI, the investment buzz, and what it all means for you.
summary: Jimmy and Matt go deep on Meta's Llama 3.1 release — including the 405B frontier-class open weights model — and the open versus closed source debate, covering Zuckerberg's stated rationale, national-security fears and universal jailbreaks. They also dissect the CrowdStrike outage, whether LLM architecture has maxed out, and whether AI investment has hit the hype-cycle plateau.
keyTalkingPoints: Llama 3.1's 405B parameter model matched or beat closed models on benchmarks — the gap between open and closed source has effectively closed
Zuckerberg's pitch: Meta does not need to sell models; open source builds its ecosystem and undermines competitors selling $20 subscriptions
Universal jailbreaks work on any closed model, so closed-source security claims fail — the best model is also the most dangerous
The CrowdStrike outage was a cascade of basic errors — a null pointer in a kernel driver — and Matt questions whether it was really an accident
On hype: Jimmy believes capability is plateauing and the next investment wave awaits genuinely productive agentic applications, with US investors also waiting out the election

jimmy: Open source has essentially caught closed source, and that should have OpenAI and Anthropic worried
LLM capability is plateauing — the models approximate human output well but generate nothing genuinely original
Current LLM architecture will not reach genuine AGI or produce new biological threats
Agentic models, not AGI, will drive the next wave of AI investment and performance
matt: No one can stay number one for more than weeks — good-enough open models will win on price, fine-tuning and independence
China will almost catch up, and almost-good-enough will be good enough for most uses
Control of Nvidia GPUs is the new oil — the decisive geopolitical resource of the AI era
Closed-source security is undermined by universal jailbreaks, so neither open nor closed is a definitive answer

title: The Sustainability Series: Unlocking AI for Accessibility with Amy Aisha Brown
description: Send us Fan Mail Unlock the secrets of how AI can transform our world into a more inclusive and accessible place with Amy Aisha Brown from King's College London. Gain invaluable insights into how enhanced accessibility benefits not only individuals with disabilities but also the wider society, particularly as we age. Learn how AI is revolutionizing learning environments and making everyday experiences more navigable for everyone. Discover the practical applications of AI tools that are already making a difference in our daily lives. From Be My (AI Eyes) to Text-to-Signlanguage, from the advanced captioning features of Microsoft Teams to ChatGPT's ability to provide helpful prompts for the neurodivergent, we highlight how AI is improving both personal and professional interactions. We explore the potential of AI in areas like online counseling and apps like Character AI, with unique bespoke AI personalities, making digital experiences more efficient and comfortable for users. We don't shy away from the ethical and societal implications of AI in accessibility. This episode dives into the complexities of bias, privacy concerns, technological dependence, vulnerability and the need for robust regulations. We emphasize the importance of political engagement to ensure AI developments align with human values. Tune in for a balanced discussion on the promises and pitfalls of AI, and why maintaining human-centered options is crucial in our rapidly evolving digital landscape. Speech Accessibility Project (illinois.edu) Be My Eyes - See the world together
summary: Amy Aisha Brown, a learning technologist at King's College London, joins the sustainability series to explore AI and accessibility — how assistive tech, real-time captions, Be My Eyes' AI shift and sign-language research are expanding participation, alongside the risks of bias, privacy exploitation and a cheap 'this will do' race to the bottom that abandons human support.

title: PODCAST RELAUNCH: It's time to urgently act on mitigating existential threats of AI
description: Send us Fan Mail "Preparing for AI" relaunches this week as the AI Podcast for Everybody. We are broadening our mission to raise awareness and to empower listeners to act on helping to stop the existential threat of unmitigated frontier model development. But is AI reallya looming existential threat or an overhyped fantasy? This episode of "Preparing for AI" tackles this provocative question, offering insights into safety, governance and alignment issues of AI development. Our discussion spans the dual concerns surrounding an omnipotent AI already influencing powerhouses like OpenAI and the possibility that current advancements are merely overblown projections. We dive into the dire warnings from experts, highlighting estimates that predict up 20%, 50& adn even 99.99% chances of AI threatening humanity. Amidst these fears, we emphasize the critical need for AI development that aligns with societal well-being, especially given unchecked models and the growing military applications of AI technology. We draw urgent parallels between AI governance and immediate global challenges like climate change and public health. Two paths to avert a dystopian future are explored: a catastrophic AI incident sparking global backlash, or a dramatic shift in public sentiment urging swift governmental action. Our goal is to galvanize awareness and activism, urging listeners to influence policymakers. For those eager to dive deeper, we recommend the illuminating content of Robert Miles and Blue Dot’s comprehensive AI courses. We scrutinize Microsoft's massive stake in OpenAI and the shift in OpenAI's board dynamics, leading to the exit of members with ethical concerns. The competitive landscape among tech giants like Google, Meta, and Anthropic is dissected, revealing the intertwining of ethical dilemmas and profit motives. Nvidia's rise due to its pivotal role in the AI boom is also examined. We stress the necessity of government and public intervention given the slim chances of self-regulation by these corporations.
